name: Kathara
what_it_is: Kathara is a lightweight network emulation system based on Docker containers, functioning as the successor to Netkit. Each network device runs as an isolated container interconnected via virtual Layer 2 LANs, enabling full network topology simulation.
components: Python API for programmatic scenario creation
CLI tool (kathara lstart, kathara lclean, etc.)
Pre-built Docker images: Quagga, FRRouting, BIND, P4, OpenVSwitch
configuration: lab.conf file defines network topology and device interconnections
Per-device *.startup scripts run at container boot
Python API for programmatic network scenario creation
Custom Docker images can be specified per device
modes: Local mode: scenarios run on local Docker engine
Megalos mode: scenarios deployed on Kubernetes cluster
CLI-driven: interactive management via kathara commands
API-driven: programmatic control via Python library
constraints: No built-in traffic measurement or packet capture tooling — relies on tools installed inside container images
No native fault injection primitives — link failures must be simulated by manually removing virtual interfaces or stopping containers
Kubernetes (Megalos) mode requires a pre-configured cluster; not suitable for fully offline or air-gapped single-host use without Docker
Network scenarios are file-system-bound directories; no GUI or web-based topology editor is included
notable_absences: No docker-compose file — Kathara manages its own container lifecycle directly via the Docker SDK
No built-in traffic generation or load tooling
No REST API or web dashboard
No native packet loss / latency / jitter injection controls
